- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot actual price spikes, then fail to sustain or correctly adjust downward afterward.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends — fails to recognize that prices often return to prior levels after sharp spikes.
- Late-period forecasts (last 10–15 days) show higher accuracy, suggesting model calibration improves with longer-term context.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often misses downward momentum until it’s already embedded in the forecast.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility — overreacts to short-term noise, especially in the first 10 days.
- Model underestimates the persistence of upward trends — fails to recognize that price increases often continue for 3–5 days after initial spike.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” sharp declines — underestimates the magnitude of drops, especially in the first 5 days.
- Model overconfident in short-term forecasts — often fails to account for structural or regulatory shifts that affect price direction.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the true price trend is trending upward — underperforms when prices are consolidating or declining.
